---
name: check-for-running-ninja-before-nohup-build
description: 2026-10-21 one idle session left four overlapping nohup Release builds in one build dir, pegging all 12 cores for an hour; pgrep ninja on the build dir before launching, and kill your builds before ending a turn
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-21 Kenneth's Mac ran at load average 32 on 12 cores for over an hour. The cause was one Claude session (the "Show MCP edits without an agent" worktree session) that launched four `nohup cmake --build … --config Release` runs between 10:56 and 11:05 into the same build dir (`.claude/worktrees/mcp-external-edits/build/arm64`), three with identical target sets. Each ninja spawned ~12 clang jobs, so 56 clang processes fought over 12 cores and every build crawled. The session had gone idle at 11:13 with its work already committed, and the builds kept running as orphans (parent pid 1) because of nohup.

**Why:** a nohup'd build survives the Bash tool timeout (see [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]]), so re-launching "the build" after each timeout adds a build instead of resuming one. ninja does not lock the build dir; concurrent instances just duplicate work and thrash.

**How to apply:**
- Before any `nohup cmake --build`, run `pgrep -fl 'ninja -f' ` and `lsof -a -d cwd -p <pid>`; if a ninja already has that build dir as cwd, tail its log instead of starting another.
- Never launch the same target set twice; wait on the saved PID with `kill -0` (see [[pgrep-wait-loop-matches-itself]]).
- Before ending a turn with the task done, kill builds you started that nobody will read (`pkill -P <ninja pid>; kill <ninja pid>`), or say in the recap that one is still running and why.
- To find who owns a stray build: the ninja's stdout path (`lsof -p <pid> -d 1`) contains the Claude Code session id; `ps -o args= -p $(pgrep -f -- "--resume=<id>")` shows the app session's side-session-notes path.

- That session launched the builds with nohup between 10:56 and 11:05 this morning, after earlier attempts hit the Bash tool timeout. Each relaunch added a build instead of resuming one, since ninja does not lock its build directory.

content.text:
The four runaway builds are dead and no compiler processes remain. The machine should feel normal within a few minutes as the load average decays.

**What I did**

- Killed the four ninja build drivers that were working in the mcp-external-edits worktree, along with every process beneath them, and then swept up the compiler processes they had orphaned. The first attempt failed because macOS's `pkill -P` needs a pattern argument and ninja ignores SIGTERM while compilers are running, so I used SIGKILL on the full subtree.
- Nothing else was stopped. The session that started the builds is idle and its change is already committed, so no work was lost.

**Where things stand**

- ninja and clang process counts are both zero.
- One minute after the kill the load average was still around 29, down from 32. That number is a trailing average, so it lags the real drop. The biggest remaining users were Spotlight indexing and Time Machine, both of which come and go on their own.
- One short-lived process named `entire` showed up at the top briefly. That is the checkpoint tool this repository runs after sessions edit files, and it exits on its own.
